name: gpa-calculator-mcp
description: GPA calculator MCP server for AI apps. Calculate GPA, CGPA, SGPA, weighted GPA, weighted grades, a target GPA, grades on the final, letter grade conversion and converting a GPA between scales. Works offline, no account.

tools.name: calculate_gpa
tools.description: Calculate a GPA from a list of courses with credits and grades, optionally weighted with a credit multiplier on each course, and optionally combined with an earlier GPA and credit total. The GPA for the courses you pass is the term GPA, and adding earlier work with prior_gpa and prior_credits gives the cumulative GPA. Inputs: courses (each with credits greater than 0, a grade that is a letter like "B+" or a percentage like 87, and an optional credit_multiplier greater than 0 such as 1.1 for an AP class), a scale id, and optional prior_gpa and prior_credits to fold in earlier terms. A credit_multiplier above 1 gives a course more weight in the weighted GPA, and when any course has one other than 1 the tool also returns weighted_gpa and weighted_credits. The term GPA still uses the plain credits. Pass drop_lowest to leave the lowest graded courses out of the GPA, as schools do that drop the lowest course; the dropped courses are named in dropped_courses. Pass prior_gpa and prior_credits together, or leave both out. Passing only one of the two is an error, so the tool says which one is missing. Alternatively, pass transcript_csv as a CSV string with columns for course name, credits, grade and optional credit multiplier; a header row is optional, the columns can be in any order, and header names like Course Title, Final Grade and Credit Hours are read as the name, grade and credits columns. When courses is not given, transcript_csv is parsed and used as the course list. In transcript_csv, a P is read as pass, NP as not pass and W as withdrawn. Those rows are left out of the GPA and named in the answer, except where the scale gives the letter points, such as P on australia-hd. Example prompt: "What's my GPA if I got an A in 3 credits, a B+ in 4 credits and a C in 3 credits?"

parameters.name: courses
parameters.description: The courses to include. Each needs credits (greater than 0) and a grade (a letter like "B+" or a percentage like 87). name is optional, and so is credit_multiplier (greater than 0), which gives a course more weight in the weighted GPA. Required when transcript_csv is not given.

credits.description: Credits for the course, must be greater than 0.

grade.description: A letter like "B+" or a percentage like 87 or "87%".

credit_multiplier.description: Optional multiplier on the credits for a weighted GPA, greater than 0, like 1.1 for an AP class. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: transcript_csv
parameters.description: A CSV string with columns for course name, credits, grade and optional credit multiplier. A header row is optional, the columns can be in any order, and header names like Course Title, Final Grade and Credit Hours are read as the name, grade and credits columns. P, NP and W grades are left out of the GPA. When courses is not given, this is parsed and used as the course list. Example: "Course,Credits,Grade\nCalculus,4,A\nHistory,3,B+"

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: Grade scale id: "us4", "us4plus", "ontario-college", "uk-classification", "australia-hd" or "weighted-5.0". Defaults to "us4". Ask the student which one their school uses if unsure.

parameters.name: prior_gpa
parameters.description: GPA from earlier terms, 0 to 7. Pass this together with prior_credits to get a cumulative GPA. Passing only one of the two is an error.

parameters.name: prior_credits
parameters.description: Credits from earlier terms, 0 or more. Pass this together with prior_gpa to get a cumulative GPA. Passing only one of the two is an error.

parameters.name: drop_lowest
parameters.description: Number of courses with the lowest grade points to leave out of the GPA, 0 or more, for schools that drop the lowest course. It must be less than the number of graded courses. Ties go to the course listed first. Defaults to 0.

tools.output: One line per course ("Calculus: A, 4.0 points x 3 credits"), then "GPA for these courses: 3.12 across 10 credits (US 4.0 scale)." With a credit multiplier on a course, the line adds the multiplier and the answer adds the weighted GPA and weighted credits. Pass prior_gpa and prior_credits together to also get the cumulative GPA. Passing only one of the two is an error and says which one is missing. Rows with P, NP or W grades in transcript_csv are left out of the GPA and named in a line that starts "Not counted in the GPA:".
tools.structured_output: scale, scale_name, courses, credits, term_gpa, gpa_credits, excluded_courses (the P, NP and W courses left out of the GPA, with name, credits and grade), dropped_courses (the courses left out by drop_lowest, with name, credits and the letter they counted as), weighted_gpa and weighted_credits when a credit multiplier other than 1 is passed, and cumulative_gpa and cumulative_credits when the earlier work is folded in. The courses array holds one entry per course with name, credits, letter, points and quality_points, plus credit_multiplier, weighted_credits and weighted_quality_points when the course has a multiplier other than 1.

tools.name: convert_grade
tools.description: Convert a letter or percentage into the matching letter, percentage range and grade points on a grade scale. Inputs: grade (a letter like "B+" or a percentage like 87 or "87%") and a scale id. Example prompt: "Convert 78 percent to a letter grade on the Ontario college scale."

parameters.name: grade
parameters.description: A letter like "B+" or a percentage like 87 or "87%".

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: Grade scale id: "us4", "us4plus", "ontario-college", "uk-classification", "australia-hd" or "weighted-5.0". Defaults to "us4". Ask the student which one their school uses if unsure.

tools.output: "78 is B+ on the Ontario college 4.0 scale (common version, check your school's table). That letter covers 75 to 79 percent and is worth 3.5 grade points."
tools.structured_output: scale, scale_name, letter, min_percent, max_percent and points.

tools.name: convert_gpa_scale
tools.description: Convert a GPA on one grade scale to the nearest band on another, so a GPA from one country can be read as a UK class or an Australian grade. Inputs: gpa (the GPA to convert, 0 to 7 and at or below the top of from_scale), from_scale (the scale the GPA is on, default us4) and optional to_scale (the scale to convert to; leave it out to convert to both the uk-classification and australia-hd scales). The GPA is read as a share of the top grade point on its own scale, then the nearest band on the target scale is returned with its percentage range and grade points. This is a common comparison, not an official conversion, so check the target school's table. Example prompt: "I have a 3.5 GPA on the US 4.0 scale. What is that in the UK?"

parameters.name: gpa
parameters.description: The GPA to convert, between 0 and 7. It must be at or below the top grade point of from_scale.

parameters.name: from_scale
parameters.description: Grade scale id the GPA is on: "us4", "us4plus", "ontario-college", "uk-classification", "australia-hd" or "weighted-5.0". Defaults to "us4".

parameters.name: to_scale
parameters.description: Grade scale id to convert to: "us4", "us4plus", "ontario-college", "uk-classification", "australia-hd" or "weighted-5.0". Leave it out to convert to both the uk-classification and australia-hd scales.

tools.output: One line for each target scale with the band, its percentage range and its grade points, then a note that this is a common comparison and not an official conversion. With no to_scale, the answer covers the uk-classification and australia-hd scales.
tools.structured_output: gpa, from_scale, from_scale_name, from_max_points and conversions. The conversions array holds one entry per target scale with scale, scale_name, letter, min_percent, max_percent and points.

tools.name: needed_on_final
tools.description: Calculate the score needed on a final exam or last assignment to reach a target course grade. Inputs: current_percent (the average on all the other work, 0 to 100), final_weight_percent (how much the final is worth, greater than 0 and at most 100) and a target. Give the target as target_percent (the course grade you want, 0 to 100), as target_letter (a letter like "B+" or a class like "2:1", whose cutoff comes from the scale table), or as both. The scale id sets the table the letter cutoff comes from. Says so when the target is already locked in or out of reach. Example prompt: "My grade is 85% and the final is worth 40% of the course. What do I need on the final to finish with a B+?"

parameters.name: current_percent
parameters.description: Current grade on the work already done, as a percentage between 0 and 100.

parameters.name: final_weight_percent
parameters.description: How much the final is worth, greater than 0 and at most 100, as a percentage of the whole course.

parameters.name: target_percent
parameters.description: The course grade you want to finish with, as a percentage between 0 and 100. Leave it out when you pass target_letter.

parameters.name: target_letter
parameters.description: The letter grade you want to finish with, like "B+" or "2:1", read from the scale table. Leave it out when you pass target_percent.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: Grade scale id: "us4", "us4plus", "ontario-college", "uk-classification", "australia-hd" or "weighted-5.0". Defaults to "us4". Ask the student which one their school uses if unsure.

tools.output: "You need 90% on the final (worth 40%) to finish with the grade B+, which starts at 87% on the US 4.0 scale. You have 85% on the rest of the course." Give target_percent 80 instead of a letter and the tool says you need 72.5% on the final to finish with 80%.
tools.structured_output: scale, scale_name, current_percent, final_weight_percent, target_percent, needed_percent, possible and already_there, plus target_letter and letter_min_percent when a letter target was given.

tools.name: weighted_grade
tools.description: Combine weighted course parts into the grade so far, plus the worst and best possible finish. Inputs: parts (each with a name, a weight that is a percentage of the whole course greater than 0, and an optional score between 0 and 100; leave the score out for parts that are not marked yet). Optional target_percent sets a course grade to work out the average needed on the unmarked parts. A weight is a percentage of the whole course, so the parts are never rescaled. Parts that add up to less than 100 leave the rest of the course still to come, and weights that add up to more than 100 are an error. Example prompt: "My course is 20% quizzes, 30% labs, 50% exam. I have 85 on quizzes and 70 on labs. What's my grade so far and what's the best I can finish with?"

parameters.name: parts
parameters.description: The weighted parts of the course. Each needs a name and a weight (a percentage of the whole course greater than 0); score is 0 to 100, or leave it out for parts that are not marked yet. Weights are percentages of the whole course, so parts that add up to less than 100 leave the rest of the course still to come.

weight.description: Weight as a percentage of the whole course, greater than 0.

score.description: Score between 0 and 100 for marked parts, or leave out for unmarked parts.

parameters.name: target_percent
parameters.description: Optional target course grade in percent. When given, works out the average needed on the unmarked parts.

tools.output: One line per part ("Quizzes: weight 20%, 85%"), then "Grade so far: 76% on the 50% of the course that is marked. That banks 38 of the 100 points the course is worth.", then the worst and best possible finish (38% and 88%) and how much of the course is still to come.
tools.structured_output: parts, total_weight, done_weight, remaining_weight, current_grade, earned_points, worst_finish, best_finish, needed_percent, possible and already_there. The parts array holds one entry per part with name, weight and score.

tools.name: target_gpa_planner
tools.description: Plan the GPA needed on upcoming credits to reach a target cumulative GPA. Inputs: current_gpa (0 to 7), credits_completed (0 or more), target_gpa (0 to 7), upcoming_credits (greater than 0) and a scale id, which sets the top grade point the scale allows. Says so when the target is already reached or would take more than one term. Example prompt: "I have a 3.1 GPA over 60 credits. What GPA do I need next semester to reach 3.4?"

parameters.name: current_gpa
parameters.description: Your cumulative GPA so far, between 0 and 7.

parameters.name: credits_completed
parameters.description: Credits already completed, 0 or more.

parameters.name: target_gpa
parameters.description: The cumulative GPA you want to reach, between 0 and 7.

parameters.name: upcoming_credits
parameters.description: Credits you will take next, greater than 0.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: Grade scale id: "us4", "us4plus", "ontario-college", "uk-classification", "australia-hd" or "weighted-5.0". Defaults to "us4". Ask the student which one their school uses if unsure.

tools.output: "You would need 4.6 on the next 15 credits, but the top of this scale is 4.0. Reaching 3.4 would take more than one term." Ask for 3.2 instead of 3.4 and the same call needs a 3.60 GPA.
tools.structured_output: scale, scale_name, current_gpa, credits_completed, target_gpa, upcoming_credits, needed_gpa, max_points, possible and already_there.

tools.name: plan_courses
tools.description: Plan the grade needed in each upcoming course to reach a target cumulative GPA. Inputs: current_gpa (0 to 7), credits_completed (0 or more), target_gpa (0 to 7), courses (each with an optional name and credits greater than 0) and a scale id, which sets the top grade point the scale allows. It works out the GPA the upcoming credits need, then gives the lowest letter in each course that keeps the plan on track, assuming the other courses meet the same target. Says so when the target is already reached or would take more than one term. Example prompt: "I have a 3.4 GPA over 60 credits. What do I need in each of my four classes next semester to reach 3.5?"

parameters.name: current_gpa
parameters.description: Your cumulative GPA so far, between 0 and 7.

parameters.name: credits_completed
parameters.description: Credits already completed, 0 or more.

parameters.name: target_gpa
parameters.description: The cumulative GPA you want to reach, between 0 and 7.

parameters.name: courses
parameters.description: The upcoming courses to plan for. Each needs credits greater than 0, and name is optional.

credits.description: Credits for the course, must be greater than 0.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: Grade scale id: "us4", "us4plus", "ontario-college", "uk-classification", "australia-hd" or "weighted-5.0". Defaults to "us4". Ask the student which one their school uses if unsure.

tools.output: "You need a 4.00 GPA over the next 12 credits to reach a cumulative 3.5 (from 3.4 over 60 credits). If every course meets or beats its target below, you reach it." Then one line per course, such as "Calculus: A or better (93% and up, 4.0 points)". When the target is already reached, every course can be any grade that keeps the average at or above it. When the needed GPA is above the top of the scale, each line says that no grade on the scale is enough.
tools.structured_output: scale, scale_name, current_gpa, credits_completed, target_gpa, upcoming_credits, needed_gpa, max_points, possible, already_there and courses. The courses array holds one entry per course with name and credits, plus target_letter, target_min_percent and target_points when the target can be reached.

tools.name: list_scales
tools.description: List the built-in grade scales with their letters, percentage ranges and grade points. Inputs: none. Example prompt: "Show me the grade scales you have built in."
tools.output: The six scales from the gradeScales list below, one line per letter with the percentage range and the grade points.
tools.structured_output: scales, an array with one entry per scale. Each entry has id, name and a bands array, and each band has letter, min_percent, max_percent and points.

gradeScales.name: Ontario college 4.0 scale (common version, check your school's table)
UK degree classification (standard boundaries, check your school's table)
Australian 7.0 scale (HD is 7, common version, check your school's table)
US weighted 5.0 scale (A is 5.0, one point above us4, check your school's table)
